SMTO-UI-0018 — A default header has no name or is listed twice

GUID: 40c30397-a2a2-4c7d-892e-dab8a5e1ddde
Slug: ui-header-name-conflict
Domain: UI · Subsystem: ui

What happened

  • This connection's extra headers, the labeled values sent with every request, include one with no name or two with the same name. The connection wasn't saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In Parameter Store, open this connection, then Advanced connection settings. Look at each Default header row. The problem is in one of these rows.
  2. Fill in a Header name for any row that's empty, or remove that row with Remove item. A header can't be sent without a name.
  3. If two rows have the same name, even with different capital letters (like Accept and accept), keep one and remove the other, then select Save. Websites treat header names the same regardless of capitals, so each name can appear only once.

What success looks like

  • The connection saves without this message.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied error details to the person who manages this connection, along with the list of headers you need.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Default-header editing found an HTTP header row with an empty name, or a name that duplicates another row when compared case-insensitively.

What this means

  • Default-header editing finds an empty header name or duplicates another name without regard to case. The shown control rejects this local action before its dependent submission. Earlier requests and saved state are unaffected by this validation result; server-side authority remains authoritative.

Why this can happen

  • Default-header editing finds an empty header name or duplicates another name without regard to case.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare header names case-insensitively while keeping secret values private.

How to fix it

  • advancedEditor() in http_profile_editor.js requires every default_headers row to have a nonempty name that is unique case-insensitively (for example Accept and accept collide). Rename, merge or remove the conflicting rows, then save the Parameter.
  • Give each default header a nonempty unique name; names are compared without case.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Each default header has one nonempty unique name.

What not to do

  • Do not repeatedly submit the same invalid input; correct the named constraint first.

Technical notes

  • The shown control rejects this local action before its dependent submission. Earlier requests and saved state are unaffected by this validation result; server-side authority remains authoritative.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
